about: Generated by plan/registry.py from plan/controls.yaml, EPICS/Db and the st.cmd files. Do not edit.

TDK:voltage:setpoint.note: no echo record: voltage:read follows while the output is on

TDK:current:setpoint.note: no echo record: current:read follows while the output is on

TDK:power:get.desc: Output power, measured V x I

REK-1:voltage:setpoint.note: until the first contact with the supply after an IOC start a write is not sent (simulation mode); then the set point takes over the supply's setting

REK-1:current:limit.note: the current LIMIT (alias current:setpoint, the lab's name). Restored at the start by autosave and sent at the first contact, on every write, with every switch-on, and every 5 s while not applied. A write is also saved (limits.sav, within 5 s): a test reads the value first and writes it back. Test range in A, within the full scale (24 A)

REK-1:_limit:apply.desc: Sends a limit not yet applied (internal)

REK-1:SetToggleOutput.desc: Set value for enabling PS output
REK-1:SetToggleOutput.note: latches: losing the permit switches the output off and sets this to 0, a 1 written while the permit is lost is cleared at once, nothing switches on by itself. The permit acts 5 s after the first contact. On: REN, limit, RST, SW1; off: REN, RST, SW0. While the permit is lost and the supply reports its output on (a direct write of ToggleOutput, the front panel, a lost off command), the off sequence is sent again every 2 s (_permit:enforce, which counts them). A request that follows the previous one within the switching time (some tens of ms) is not lost: it is sent when the switching record is free, within 1 s (_out:resend)

REK-1:OutputIntlk.desc: Forces the output off, permit open

REK-1:ToggleOutput.desc: Toggle the status of the PS output

REK-1:status:read.note: OFF, ON (remote), OFF, LOCAL and ON, LOCAL (MINOR: front panel in control)

dis_loop.name: Discharge current loop
dis_loop.model: PID loop: records EPICS/Db/loop.db, algorithm in the service loops/mist2loop

flags.assumed: The default gains come from the plant model of the emulation, not from MIST-2 (docs/emulation/LOOP.md)

LOOP-DIS:mode:setpoint.note: the operator's request, accepted by the IOC itself (mode:get shows the mode, which needs more than the request); cleared (MANUAL) by the service when it hands back or refuses and by the IOC when the service is not alive (latch). A test writes only MANUAL: PID would act on the filament heating

LOOP-DIS:mode:get.note: PID only while requested, accepted by the service and the service alive

LOOP-DIS:reason:get.note: why the loop last handed back or refused, until the next request

LOOP-DIS:service:get.note: 1 while the loop service's counter changes within the watchdog time, else 0 (MAJOR)

LOOP-DIS:permit1:get.note: permit condition 1 as words: fulfilled, the condition's words (not fulfilled, no alarm), no data (INVALID: its PV INVALID or not connected)

LOOP-DIS:value:read.note: the measured value as the loop reads it

LOOP-DIS:limit:get.desc: Output held back by a limit
LOOP-DIS:limit:get.note: free, at minimum, at maximum (MINOR) or slew limited

LOOP-DIS:output:get.note: in PID the service's output, in MANUAL the actuator's set point

LOOP-DIS:value:setpoint.note: soft setting of the IOC (no device: accepted by the IOC itself), saved by autosave; clamped to [spmin, spmax]

LOOP-DIS:spmin:setpoint.note: set point minimum, saved by autosave; moved above the set point, it brings the set point up to it

LOOP-DIS:spmax:setpoint.note: set point maximum, saved by autosave (default 23 A, our choice, to be confirmed); moved below the set point, it brings the set point down to it

THM:channels.note: full text in the field VAL$ (more than 40 characters)

logger.name: Data logger
logger.model: Channel Access logger logger/mist2log (Python, pyepics) on TimescaleDB, Grafana

LOGGER:count:get.note: +1 per second, written by the logger

LOGGER:alive:get.note: 1 while the counter changed within 5 s, else 0 (MAJOR): the logger is dead or cannot reach this IOC

LOGGER:disconnected:get.note: MINOR while any logged PV is not connected

LOGGER:db:get.note: unknown (no logger since the IOC start), connected, lost (MAJOR)

LOGGER:buffer:get.note: share of the buffer in use while the database is lost or slow: MINOR from 50 %, MAJOR from 90 %

LOGGER:dropped:get.note: rows that did not fit into the buffer since the logger started (MINOR from the first; each loss is an event)
